chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Hasan al-Lu'lu'i from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Musaddif who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does a woman perform Hajj on behalf of a man? He said: 'Yes, if she is a pious Muslim woman and she has already performed Hajj. There are many women who are better than a man.'
ai.seo_question: Can a woman perform Hajj on behalf of a man according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a woman may perform Hajj on behalf of a man, provided she is a *faqihah* (juristically knowledgeable) Muslim and has already fulfilled her own obligatory Hajj. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual and intellectual capacity of women, concluding with the profound ethical observation that 'many a woman is better than a man,' challenging rigid gender hierarchies in religious merit.
